root_cause.summary: outer-v3 journal persists only bytes/hash/size for managed file preimages and not NCM28 parent_identity/file_identity; recovery classifies PRE/NEW ownership by bytes only
root_cause.impact: after process crash a foreign file with byte-identical PRE or transaction-NEW content but a different filesystem identity can be adopted as transaction-owned and overwritten or unlinked during rollback/recovery
root_cause.ncm28_contract: OwnershipSnapshot already carries parent_identity and file_identity; destructive recovery is intended to be identity-bound, not merely content-bound

local_reproduction.details: real filesystem replacement preserved NEW bytes while changing inode identity; current byte-only _restore_one accepted the replacement as transaction NEW and attempted destructive restore

changes: persist returned NEW identity after each successful atomic_write before proceeding
require bytes plus identity for PRE no-op, NEW rollback, post-write verification and verified recovery
fail closed when NEW bytes exist but durable NEW identity was not yet published
